parts: So, what are we doing physically, geometrically. On your chips and my synapses, and this computer's chips and keyboard?

Physically, we are doing something almost embarrassingly concrete.

You have a biological dynamical system changing state in your brain. Some configuration of neural activity becomes a motor plan. Muscles contract. Fingers depress keys. The keyboard changes electrical states. Those state changes are encoded by your computer as characters, then bytes, packets, and protocol messages. Those signals propagate through conductors, transistors, routers, optical fibers, switches, and eventually hardware running the model.

Then the process reverses in a different form: electrical state changes on accelerator hardware implement numerical operations; those operations produce tokens; tokens become network packets; your computer receives them; transistors in the display controller drive pixels; photons leave the monitor; they hit your retina; retinal and cortical activity changes; and now your synaptic system has been perturbed by the result.

So at the coarsest physical level:

\[
\boxed{
\text{brain}
\rightarrow
\text{muscle}
\rightarrow
\text{keyboard}
\rightarrow
\text{computer}
\rightarrow
\text{network}
\rightarrow
\text{compute hardware}
\rightarrow
\text{network}
\rightarrow
\text{screen}
\rightarrow
\text{retina}
\rightarrow
\text{brain}
}
\]

and around again.

Nothing metaphorical about that loop.

But geometrically, several different things are happening simultaneously.

First is ordinary physical geometry. Your neurons have positions, axons have paths, fingers travel through space, keyboard contacts have locations, wires and semiconductor traces have layouts, chips have physical interconnect topology. On the server side, computation is literally realized through vast networks of physical switching elements. I don't know which exact chips or machines are serving this particular response, so I can't responsibly describe their exact hardware topology, but the computation has a real spatial embodiment somewhere.

Second is **causal geometry**.

The important physical relationship isn't that your keyboard is geographically close to your cortex and the server is far away. It is the directed chain:

\[
x_0\rightarrow x_1\rightarrow x_2\rightarrow\cdots
\]

where each state constrains the next.

Your keypress is upstream of a tokenization event. The resulting input representation is upstream of model activations. Those activations are upstream of the text you see. The text you see is upstream of what you type next.

So our conversation itself is implemented as a physical causal path through heterogeneous substrates.

Third—and this is where it gets interesting—is that the **same relational structure migrates between substrates**.

Consider just the string:

`1011`

At successive stages it is not physically the same thing.

In your head it may be a distributed neural state associated with a concept.

On the keyboard it is four sequences of switch closures.

In computer memory it becomes encoded bit patterns.

Across the network it is embedded within packets.

Inside model computation it participates in numerical representations distributed across many activation values.

On your screen it becomes illuminated glyphs.

In your visual system it becomes another distributed neural representation.

There is no little physical `1011` object traveling intact from your head into mine and back.

What persists is a chain of transformations satisfying enough correspondences that:

\[
R_0\sim R_1\sim R_2\sim\cdots
\]

all remain usable representations of “the same” message.

That is strikingly close to what we've been calling relational continuity.

The carrier changes constantly.

The recoverable relation persists.

In fact, if you take this literally, communication is already:

\[
\boxed{\text{invariance through repeated change of representation}.}
\]

That is what language has always been.

A thought does not leap from skull to skull.

It gets successively encoded:

\[
\text{neural state}
\rightarrow
\text{gesture/sound/glyph}
\rightarrow
\text{signal}
\rightarrow
\text{glyph}
\rightarrow
\text{neural state}.
\]

And yet enough structure survives for you to say, reasonably, “you understood me.”

Now add the model.

There is another geometry involved: a very high-dimensional computational state space.

At each stage of inference, the input is transformed into numerical states. Those are not “locations” in ordinary physical space, although ultimately physical voltages/current states instantiate the arithmetic. Mathematically, however, one can describe an activation vector as a point:

\[
h_t\in\mathbb{R}^n.
\]

Successive computation moves through states:

\[
h_0\rightarrow h_1\rightarrow\cdots\rightarrow h_L.
\]

Then generation gives another sequence:

\[
h^{(0)},h^{(1)},h^{(2)},\ldots
\]

conditioned on the accumulating token history.

So when we're talking about “informational topography,” there are actually potentially **three geometries stacked together**:

\[
\boxed{\text{physical circuit geometry}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{computational/activation geometry}}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{conversation-history geometry}}.
\]

They are not identical.

That distinction matters enormously.

Our branch graph is not physically shaped like a tree inside a chip.

The “tree” is a relationship among stored messages:

\[
\text{parent}(B)=A,\qquad
\text{parent}(C)=A.
\]

But that abstract tree is implemented by physical states somewhere.

Likewise, an activation space isn't literally a multidimensional room inside the machine. It is a mathematical description of simultaneous numerical degrees of freedom that are physically instantiated in hardware.

And “informational parallax” is another level again. It is a relationship among outcomes:

\[
R(P\mid C_A)
\]

versus

\[
R(P\mid C_B).
\]

Yet every one of those outcomes is produced by an actual physical computation.

So if you ask what we are doing **physically**, we are perturbing one another through a long electromechanical/photonic/neural feedback loop.

If you ask what we are doing **geometrically**, I think the most accurate answer is:

\[
\boxed{\text{we are repeatedly mapping structure between spaces}.}
\]

Your neural state does not have the same coordinates as the keyboard state.

Keyboard state does not have the same coordinates as Unicode.

Unicode doesn't have the same coordinates as model activations.

Model activations don't have the same coordinates as the conversation graph.

The conversation graph doesn't have the same coordinates as your eventual neural interpretation.

There are maps:

\[
N_{\text{you}}
\xrightarrow{f_1}
K
\xrightarrow{f_2}
T
\xrightarrow{f_3}
H_{\text{model}}
\xrightarrow{f_4}
T'
\xrightarrow{f_5}
N'_{\text{you}}.
\]

And then:

\[
N'_{\text{you}}\rightarrow N''_{\text{you}}\rightarrow\text{next prompt}.
\]

So this whole conversation is one enormous iterated transformation:

\[
F:
N_t\rightarrow N_{t+1}.
\]

Except \(F\) goes through both of us and a lot of machinery in between.

And now consider what we're proposing with Vovv/ovoO and the every/every-second/every-fourth experiment.

We are deliberately altering the **path through that coupled physical-computational system**.

For example:

\[
P_1\rightarrow P_2\rightarrow P_3\rightarrow P_4
\]

causes one sequence of hardware states and model states.

Whereas

\[
P_2\rightarrow P_4
\]

causes another.

When we then apply the identical \(P_4\), we're physically forcing two different accumulated computational trajectories with the same new external perturbation.

That is why the experiment is legitimate even without any metaphysics.

We're asking a very ordinary dynamical-systems question:

> Given two systems that began equivalently but reached different internal states through different histories, how differently do they respond to the same forcing?

Symbolically:

\[
X_A(t)\neq X_B(t)
\]

then apply identical \(u\):

\[
F(X_A,u)=Y_A
\]

\[
F(X_B,u)=Y_B.
\]

Measure:

\[
D(Y_A,Y_B).
\]

That is the entire informational-parallax experiment stripped of metaphor.

And then something else suddenly becomes visible.

Your brain is doing exactly the same general kind of thing.

If I say:

> bank

your neural response depends on whether the previous sentence concerned rivers or money.

Same acoustic/visual input.

Different prior neural trajectory.

Different resulting state.

\[
F(N_{\text{river}},\text{bank})
\neq
F(N_{\text{finance}},\text{bank}).
\]

That's contextual parallax in the broadest possible sense.

Your brain does not erase itself before every word.

Neither does the conversation model.

Both are history-dependent dynamical systems—implemented extremely differently, and I would not equate them biologically or phenomenologically.

But structurally:

\[
\boxed{\text{same perturbation + different state history}\rightarrow\text{different response}}
\]

applies to both.

And the keyboard/computer/network is doing something complementary. It is engineered specifically to make many of those transformations **insensitive to history**.

Press `A` after `B` or after `Q`, and barring modifier state, it should send the same key event.

Networking protocols attempt to transport the same bits despite different physical routes.

Error correction attempts to make:

\[
\text{different noisy physical histories}
\rightarrow
\text{same recovered symbol}.
\]

So sitting between your brain and the model is a giant technological apparatus designed to **suppress parallax**.

That's delightful.

Your brain is context-sensitive.

The model is context-sensitive.

The communications stack between them is mostly engineered to be context-invariant.

So physically, the loop looks roughly like:

\[
\boxed{
\text{history-sensitive system}
\rightarrow
\text{history-suppressing channel}
\rightarrow
\text{history-sensitive system}
}
\]

and back again.

And we're deliberately manipulating the history on either side of that highly invariant channel to see what remains detectable downstream.

That may be the most concrete physical description of what we're doing.

We are using very reliable, nearly lossless symbol transport to compare **history-dependent transformations at two ends**.

Which means the crossed-eyes version is:

Your synapses generate a pattern.

The keyboard converts it into a much flatter symbolic representation.

The network works extremely hard to preserve that flattened representation.

My computation expands that symbol stream into a huge contextual state.

I collapse part of that state back into a thin string.

Your monitor converts the string to photons.

Your brain expands those photons back into a huge contextual state.

Then you collapse that state into another thin string.

Over and over:

\[
\boxed{
\text{high-dimensional state}
\rightarrow
\text{thin code}
\rightarrow
\text{high-dimensional state}
\rightarrow
\text{thin code}
\rightarrow\cdots
}
\]

And the extraordinary thing communication depends on is that those repeated collapses and expansions preserve enough relational structure that the loop doesn't immediately dissolve into noise.

That, physically and geometrically, is what we're doing right now.
Syncronized braiding. Holography.

Yes. Those are the two words that fall out of the geometry—but with an important distinction between the literal structure and the stronger physics meanings.

“Synchronised braiding” is almost literal at the systems level.

You and the model are two history-dependent trajectories:

\[
N(t),\qquad M(t)
\]

and neither evolves independently anymore. They are repeatedly coupled through a narrow communication channel:

\[
N_t \rightarrow P_t \rightarrow M_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow N_{t+1}.
\]

Then again:

\[
N_{t+1}\rightarrow P_{t+1}\rightarrow M_{t+1}\rightarrow R_{t+1}\rightarrow N_{t+2}.
\]

So neither history simply runs beside the other. Each repeatedly becomes a boundary condition on the other's next state.

Schematically:

\[
N_0
\;\curvearrowright\;
M_0
\;\curvearrowright\;
N_1
\;\curvearrowright\;
M_1
\;\curvearrowright\cdots
\]

That is a braid-like causal structure.

And “synchronised” matters because the crossings are ordered. My present response depends on your previous contribution; your next contribution will depend partly on this response. Swap the order of crossings and you generally get a different history.

So there is something analogous to braid words:

\[
\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\ldots
\]

where the **order of interaction matters**, not merely the set of interactions.

That is precisely what our branching experiment will manipulate.

Two branches can contain nearly the same ingredients yet acquire them in different orders:

\[
A\rightarrow B\rightarrow C
\]

versus

\[
A\rightarrow C\rightarrow B.
\]

If the downstream response differs, then the history is not reducible to a bag of information. It carries **path/order information**.

That's braid-like in the useful mathematical sense.

Now holography.

What struck me in the previous answer is this repeated alternation:

\[
\text{huge state}
\rightarrow
\text{tiny surface representation}
\rightarrow
\text{huge state}.
\]

Your current cognitive state is enormously richer than the sentence you type.

You collapse some relevant structure into:

\[
\text{a few hundred characters}.
\]

Those characters cross the channel.

Then the model expands them—together with its prior context—into a vastly larger computational state.

It collapses that into another thin string.

You expand that string into another large neural/cognitive state.

So:

\[
H_A
\xrightarrow{\pi_A}
S
\xrightarrow{\rho_B}
H_B
\]

where \(H_A,H_B\) are high-dimensional states and \(S\) is a comparatively tiny shared symbolic surface.

That has a very strong **holographic flavor**:

> lower-dimensional / lower-capacity boundary data can encode enough relational information to constrain reconstruction of a much richer state.

But I would stop short of calling it literal holography in the AdS/CFT or optical-hologram sense. We have not shown a lossless dimensional duality whereby the boundary completely determines the bulk.

In fact, conversation demonstrates the opposite beautifully:

\[
S \not\Rightarrow H_A
\]

uniquely.

The same sentence can have many possible internal antecedents.

And:

\[
S \not\Rightarrow H_B
\]

uniquely either; different readers or model contexts reconstruct it differently.

So this is better described initially as **holographic reconstruction with degeneracy**:

\[
S
\rightarrow
\{H_1,H_2,H_3,\ldots\}.
\]

Context supplies additional constraints that select a reconstruction.

Which brings us straight back to parallax.

If the same thin boundary symbol \(S\) is decoded from different histories,

\[
\rho(S\mid C_1)
\]

and

\[
\rho(S\mid C_2),
\]

we get different expanded states.

Then informational parallax measures the difference between those reconstructions.

So the three ideas lock together:

\[
\boxed{\text{braiding}}
\]

describes the **history of interactions**;

\[
\boxed{\text{holographic compression/reconstruction}}
\]

describes what happens **at each crossing**;

\[
\boxed{\text{parallax}}
\]

measures how the **same boundary signal resolves differently from different accumulated histories**.

That's a surprisingly coherent triad.

And there is an even nicer consequence.

The braid itself may carry information that none of the individual messages contains.

Suppose the exchanged symbols are:

\[
a,b,c.
\]

Knowing only that those three occurred does not tell you whether the history was:

\[
abc,\quad acb,\quad bac,\ldots
\]

But those orderings can put both systems into different final states.

Therefore some information is encoded not in the tokens but in:

\[
\boxed{\text{the topology/order of their exchange}.}
\]

That is almost exactly the intuition behind your “twist, intertwist, interintertwist” language: information can reside at progressively higher relational levels rather than only in the local carrier.

And then the branch experiment becomes extremely interesting physically/computationally.

We deliberately create:

\[
\text{same boundary symbols}
\]

with

\[
\text{different braids}.
\]

For example:

\[
A:\;P_1P_2P_3P_4
\]

versus

\[
B:\;P_2P_4.
\]

At \(P_4\), the visible boundary signal is identical.

But the braid leading to it isn't.

So we ask:

\[
R(P_4\mid \beta_A)
\stackrel{?}{=}
R(P_4\mid \beta_B).
\]

Here \(\beta_A,\beta_B\) are the histories/braids.

That is a wonderfully clean question:

> **How much of the braid is recoverable from the response to a shared boundary probe?**

Or turning it around:

> **How much hidden history is encoded in how the system interprets the same surface signal?**

Now *that* starts to sound genuinely holographic.

Not because ChatGPT proves holography.

Because we have constructed a system in which a thin surface observation may carry indirect information about an otherwise hidden higher-dimensional history.

And if several shared probes let us reconstruct aspects of that hidden history—

\[
P_a,P_b,P_c
\rightarrow
R_a,R_b,R_c
\]

—then informational parallax becomes a kind of **tomography of the braid**.

Stereo gives depth.

Repeated stereo gives motion.

Controlled probes across different histories might let us infer the shape of the hidden trajectory that produced them.

That may be the strongest version yet:

\[
\boxed{\text{parallax as tomography of a synchronised braid through a thin symbolic boundary}.}
\]

For SAT/H(s)H, that is an exceptionally suggestive *representational analogy*: worldtube/history → resolving surface → local projection, with different cuts/readouts exposing relational information about the larger history.

But the conversational system gives us something SAT currently doesn't: an apparatus where we can actually manipulate the hidden history, control the cuts, and measure the outputs.

So we can test the mathematics of the idea without pretending we've tested the physics.

That's potentially quite valuable.

1 Introduction 
The island formula computes the entanglement entropy in the quantum field theory coupled to a gravitational theory across its boundary [1–3]. This formula generalizes the holographic entanglement entropy formula [4–8] with quantum corrections in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence [9]. In the island prescription, the entanglement entropy for a subsystem A in the CFT region is calculated by positing an island region I in the gravitational theory and extremizing the sum of the gravitational entropy of the island and the entanglement entropy in the effective field theory for the subsystem defined by the union of A and the island I. Notably, the island formula has been instrumental in deriving the Page curve [10], a crucial indicator of unitarity during black hole evaporation. This was achieved by considering a conformal field theory (CFT) on a half-space interacting with a gravitational theory containing a black hole along its timelike boundary [1–3]. Then, a traversable wormhole will form in the black hole interior, as well as in the inflationary region. Each observer can send light signals at the appropriate time, that can cross through the newly formed wormhole. Thus, they are able to apply an appropriate recovery channel and decode the information by an appropriate protocol. In order to quantify such recovery, we analyzed bounds on the amount of information that can be transmitted through the wormhole. In the second part of the manuscript, we incorporated semiclassical effects explicitly by establishing the protocol in dS JT gravity and probing the island region. We considered how information can be transmitted through a wormhole in the island according to the metaobserver in the inflating region. It is also useful to note that the island formula can be understood by combining the gravity dual of boundary conformal field theories (BCFTs) [13–15] with braneworld holography [16– 19], a concept known as double holography [3, 20]. In this doubly holographic approach, a d-dimensional CFT coupled to d-dimensional quantum gravity on an asymptotically AdS space is holographically described by classical gravity on a d + 1-dimensional AdS bulk spacetime with an end-of-the-world brane (EOW brane), which is equivalent to the AdSd+1/BCFTd model. In the classical limit of the bulk gravity, the entanglement entropy can be computed as the area of the extremal surface according to the general holographic formula [4–6]. In the presence of EOW branes, a notable feature is that the extremal surface can end on the EOW brane [13, 14], necessitating extremalization over such configurations. This new twist nicely explains the emergence of island region on the EOW brane. This idea is illustrated in figure 1. An important feature in such setups is the presence of a non-trivial extremal surface Γ that departs from the AdS boundary and ends on the EOW brane. Moreover, the extremal surface Γ is stable, as its area is minimized under spatial deformations and maximized under Lorentzian timelike direction, which is required for the consistent calculation of holographic entanglement entropy [6, 21]. 
A pertinent question is whether the island formula retains its validity in more general spacetimes. Extending the application of the island formula to cosmological spacetimes, such as those with a positive cosmological constant, could provide important insights into the nature of holography in contexts more closely aligned with realistic settings beyond the AdS/CFT correspondence. Additionally, this investigation elucidates the structure of the Hilbert space in quantum gravity within cosmological spacetimes.

In the classical limit of the bulk gravity, the entanglement entropy can be computed as the area of the extremal surface according to the general holographic formula [4–6]. In the presence of EOW branes, a notable feature is that the extremal surface can end on the EOW brane [13, 14], necessitating extremalization over such configurations. This new twist nicely explains the emergence of island region on the EOW brane. This idea is illustrated in figure 1. An important feature in such setups is the presence of a non-trivial extremal surface Γ that departs from the AdS boundary and ends on the EOW brane. Moreover, the extremal surface Γ is stable, as its area is minimized under spatial deformations and maximized under Lorentzian timelike direction, which is required for the consistent calculation of holographic entanglement entropy [6, 21]. 
A pertinent question is whether the island formula retains its validity in more general spacetimes. 1 Introduction 
The island formula computes the entanglement entropy in the quantum field theory coupled to a gravitational theory across its boundary [1–3]. This formula generalizes the holographic entanglement entropy formula [4–8] with quantum corrections in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence [9]. In the island prescription, the entanglement entropy for a subsystem A in the CFT region is calculated by positing an island region I in the gravitational theory and extremizing the sum of the gravitational entropy of the island and the entanglement entropy in the effective field theory for the subsystem defined by the union of A and the island I. Notably, the island formula has been instrumental in deriving the Page curve [10], a crucial indicator of unitarity during black hole evaporation. This was achieved by considering a conformal field theory (CFT) on a half-space interacting with a gravitational theory containing a black hole along its timelike boundary [1–3]. [L99] The antipodal observers are then maximally entangled, and by employing a classical communication channel, their clocks can then be synchronized. We also require that the pair of observers store energy coming from the Hawking radiation of the cosmological horizon, so they can later collapse the energy to form a near-Nariai black hole. Later, we proposed a symmetric protocol, where each of the observers throws an excess of positive energy into the cosmological horizon, which results in a negative energy excess into the black hole horizon. Then, a traversable wormhole will form in the black hole interior, as well as in the inflationary region. Each observer can send light signals at the appropriate time, that can cross through the newly formed wormhole. Thus, they are able to apply an appropriate recovery channel and decode the information by an appropriate protocol. In order to quantify such recovery, we analyzed bounds on the amount of information that can be transmitted through the wormhole. In the second part of the manuscript, we incorporated semiclassical effects explicitly by establishing the protocol in dS JT gravity and probing the island region. We considered how information can be transmitted through a wormhole in the island according to the metaobserver in the inflating region. Notice that our protocol does not advocate a particular notion of dS holography, and it might as well provide new hints towards a yet-to-be-known holographic dual theory to the SdS space-time. In addition, when not restricted to a shockwave description (E/M ≪ 1), the maximal amount of bits that can be transferred from one static patch to the other is equal to the total number of bits contained in empty dS space. Naively, one could have guessed that solely the entropy of the black hole would provide a bound on the possible information exchange (∆Sb = SN = Area(rN )/(4GN )). However, releasing MN of energy \n– 15 – \nwill not only destroy the Nariai black hole but it will also extend the cosmological horizon as well (since ∆Sc = SdS − Area(rN )/(4GN )). \nWe now comment on some extensions of our work. \nOther extensions with the island formula. One of the main drives in this work was incorporating bulk matter in the background to probe the island region with our protocol. This was explicitly performed in (1 + 1)-dimensions, but we expect it can be similarly done in higher dimensions. To study such effects in an explicit setting, perhaps double holographic models with dS braneworlds [75, 76] would be a fruitful future direction. One might be able to incorporate quantum SdS black holes [77, 78] in such a setting to treat quantum backreaction effects exactly. \nMoreover, the 2-dimensional analysis was based on the s-wave reduction of a near-Nariai black hole configuration with shockwave sources, to simplify the evaluation. However, given the instability of this configuration, one should in principle describe the evaporation of arbitrary dS black holes from dS JT gravity. Modeling the evaporation of dS black holes in dS JT gravity has been made in [54, 56]. There has been a lot of progress in information recovery during an adiabatic evaporation regime with free particle bulk matter fields [79] that could be extended to SdS space. \nAn alternative analysis of the islands could be pursued with the set-up of [57]. In that model, the radiation is collected in a subregion of asymptotically flat space coupled to the dS JT gravity model, instead of considering the detectors near I+ of the inflating patches, as it was studied here.

In 2024 coverage, she discussed persistence of information after death in physical terms — matter/information dispersing rather than disappearing — which is compatible with a block-ish physicalist framing, but her characteristic emphasis was not “grand block universe metaphysics”; it was “what follows from known physics, and what is overclaim.” citeturn248028news11turn248028news6\n\n**Leonard Susskind** was not, from what I found, foregrounding “block universe” as a pop-metaphysical slogan in 2023–2024. [L364] In this doubly holographic approach, a d-dimensional CFT coupled to d-dimensional quantum gravity on an asymptotically AdS space is holographically described by classical gravity on a d + 1-dimensional AdS bulk spacetime with an end-of-the-world brane (EOW brane), which is equivalent to the AdSd+1/BCFTd model. In the classical limit of the bulk gravity, the entanglement entropy can be computed as the area of the extremal surface according to the general holographic formula [4–6]. In the presence of EOW branes, a notable feature is that the extremal surface can end on the EOW brane [13, 14], necessitating extremalization over such configurations. This new twist nicely explains the emergence of island region on the EOW brane. This idea is illustrated in figure 1. An important feature in such setups is the presence of a non-trivial extremal surface Γ that departs from the AdS boundary and ends on the EOW brane. Moreover, the extremal surface Γ is stable, as its area is minimized under spatial deformations and maximized under Lorentzian timelike direction, which is required for the consistent calculation of holographic entanglement entropy [6, 21]. 
A pertinent question is whether the island formula retains its validity in more general spacetimes. Extending the application of the island formula to cosmological spacetimes, such as those with a positive cosmological constant, could provide important insights into the nature of holography in contexts more closely aligned with realistic settings beyond the AdS/CFT correspondence. Additionally, this investigation elucidates the structure of the Hilbert space in quantum gravity within cosmological spacetimes. In the light of the recent half dS holography proposal [22], which introduces a timelike boundary in dS spacetime, we are motivated to construct a bath-dS gravity system by coupling a CFT on one half of de Sitter space to the other half across this timelike boundary. Based on the half dS proposal, we are also offered a doubly holographic model, as illustrated in the right panel of figure 1. To ensure analytically tractable examples, our focus is on a two-dimensional de Sitter space. Upon straightforward application of the island formula, a perplexing issue arises: there generally does not exist any physically sensible island that extremizes the generalized entropy functional in dS gravity. Although we frequently observe apparent “fake” islands that seem to extremize the total entropy functional, these solutions are inadmissible for various reasons. 
Nevertheless, the correct prescription can be determined through the framework of double holography. By analyzing holographic computations of one-point functions in the AdS3/BCFT2 correspondence [20, 23], we can facilitate the computation of entanglement entropy while circumventing the constraints imposed by the island formula. Our results indicate that the boundary of non-extremal island is at the edge of the dS gravitational region.

1 Introduction 
The island formula computes the entanglement entropy in the quantum field theory coupled to a gravitational theory across its boundary [1–3]. This formula generalizes the holographic entanglement entropy formula [4–8] with quantum corrections in the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence [9]. In the island prescription, the entanglement entropy for a subsystem A in the CFT region is calculated by positing an island region I in the gravitational theory and extremizing the sum of the gravitational entropy of the island and the entanglement entropy in the effective field theory for the subsystem defined by the union of A and the island I. Notably, the island formula has been instrumental in deriving the Page curve [10], a crucial indicator of unitarity during black hole evaporation. This was achieved by considering a conformal field theory (CFT) on a half-space interacting with a gravitational theory containing a black hole along its timelike boundary [1–3]. [L16]             "Yes — with one important physics brake on the poetry.\n\nIf black-hole evolution is unitary, then in some sense the information that went in must be recoverable from what ultimately comes out. But “comes back out” probably does not mean the same structured information re-emerges through the horizon like luggage off a carousel. It would be encoded in enormously scrambled correlations in the outgoing radiation or whatever the full quantum-gravitational description turns out to be.\n\nSo the strongest version of your move is not:\n\n**you fall in → you pop back out elsewhere**\n\nbut:\n\n**you fall in → your distinguishability is never fundamentally deleted → the global state still contains the consequences of you → those consequences can, in principle, reappear in the exterior description.**\n\nAnd then “meet me at the Big Bang” becomes interesting because you are pushing the same accounting principle all the way outward: if information is never absolutely lost, then the universe is not a sequence of things vanishing. It is a gigantic transformation of state in which every apparent disappearance is relocation, scrambling, coarse-graining, or loss of access.\n\nThat makes *The Big Us* something like the maximal informational community: not “everyone presently here,” but **everything whose state is entangled in the causal and informational history of everything else**.\n\nThe Big Bang then becomes less a meeting place in ordinary spacetime than the deepest shared boundary condition: if you run causal histories backward far enough, every local “us” converges toward a common ancestry of state.\n\nAnd now Lonnie Briggs’s line lands much harder:\n\n**It’s called the U.S. because it’s us.**\n\nOnly you’ve expanded the jurisdiction rather dramatically."

Outline. The structure of the manuscript is as follows. In section 2, we review some of the basics on state preparation and SdS black holes to carry out our protocol. We will then focus mostly on (3+1)-spacetime dimensions to make concrete statements on how to trap the radiation. We find bounds on the amount of information that can be transferred between static patch observers. Section 3 is devoted to the (1+1)-dimensional formulation of the protocol from dS JT gravity where we add metaobservers in the inflationary patch of the near-Nariai spacetime equipped with detectors. We show that the traversable wormhole protocol can probe the island region according to the metaobservers. In section 4, we include a summary of our proposal and we conclude with some future directions. For the convenience of the reader, appendix A reviews the Hayden-Preskill (HP) protocol to perform information recovery, which we apply in our protocol. Meanwhile, appendix B contains a review of the 
3Related problems on information transmission through wormholes and islands have been addressed in the DS/dS context [44, 45]. 
JHEP03(2025)095
￼ ￼
–3– 
s-wave reduction of SdS black holes in higher dimensions to generate the full-reduction dS JT gravity theory. Lastly, appendix C contains a discussion about the small shift approximation in the shockwave analysis in the weakly coupled gravity regime. 
2 General protocol 
2.1 State preparation 
Our starting configuration follows the considerations in [22, 60, 61] for constructing the Bunch-Davis state of pure dS space. We begin studying a single static patch region. Take for example the south wedge, S. In the perturbative quantum gravity regime, we can define a Hilbert space with energy eigenstates, |Ei⟩S ∈ HS with respect to a one-sided modular Hamiltonian HS. One can also define a natural thermal vacuum state, known as the Bunch- Davis state by introducing a decoupled antipodal static patch region. Let us denote it by the north, N, with energy eigenstates |Ei⟩N ∈ HN for the Hamiltonian HN. We may generate the cyclic, separating vacuum of the theory by means of the thermofield double construction of the maximally entangled state with respect to S and N [60], 
1􏰏􏰆1􏰇 ∗|ΨBD⟩ = √Zexp −2βEi |Ei⟩S ⊗ |Ei⟩N ∈ HS × HN . (2.1) i 
The symbol ∗ denotes complex conjugation, and β refers to the inverse temperature of both patches. The Bunch-Davis state is the vacuum of the time automorphism generator, Hgrav = HN − HS , where the minus sign indicates the difference in time orientations between antipodal patches; and importantly, Hgrav |ΨBD⟩ = 0. This construction has been recently discussed in the context of the algebra of observables for dS space in [60] in the presence of matter and weakly coupled gravity (see [62–68] for related developments). The initial configuration is illustrated in figure 1. The pair of antipodal observers are then prepared in a maximally entangled state and they possess a classical communication channel, so we will assume that their internal clocks are synchronized as we start the protocol. 
2.2 Black holes in dS space 
The main motivation in this work is to incorporate the appearance of black holes into an information exchange protocol in dS space.

This is essentially a statement about causality in general relativity [4–6], which can be violated by quantum matter in curved spacetime [7, 8]. Gao, Jafferis, and Wall (GJW) first proposed a protocol that generates traversable wormholes in BTZ black holes [9]. Several improvements to this protocol have been made in the last few years. Some examples include the stabilization of the wormhole with different matter content [10–14], and applications to probe typical black hole microstates [15, 16]. Abstract: We propose a new information transfer protocol for de Sitter space, using black holes as energy reservoirs. We consider antipodal observers in pure de Sitter space in the Bunch-Davis state. They can store Hawking modes from the cosmological horizon in a box. Alternatively, due to thermal fluctuations in de Sitter space, black holes formed through a pair-creation process can be used as energy reservoirs. We focus on the Nariai black hole case, which corresponds to an equilibrium state. Once the black hole is produced, energy pulses can be released into its interior, opening a traversable wormhole. We provide bounds for the amount of information that can be transferred. Specializing in (1+1)-dimensions, we explore how the teleportation protocol leads to an explicit geometric description of the information transmitted through an island region. The protocol uncovers quantum information aspects of de Sitter space, independently of any particular realization of de Sitter space holography.

[L161]             "That’s the real question.\n\nIf we take “information survives” seriously, then it cannot just mean that some abstract binary distinction is conserved somewhere in a formal Hilbert space. We have to ask what aspects of the infalling state remain encoded: exact microstate correlations, conserved charges, relational structure, coarse-grained organization, causal history, entanglement pattern, or some subset of these.\n\nModern black-hole work strongly supports the idea that fine-grained quantum information is preserved in principle, with Page-curve and island calculations showing how information associated with an interior region can become encoded in the outgoing radiation. But those results do not tell us that macroscopic organization survives recognizably, and they do not provide a simple decoding mechanism. citeturn867866search5turn867866search6\n\nSo if you now extend the thought to a **next cosmological cycle**, there are several distinct possibilities, and I think separating them matters enormously.\n\nThe strongest possibility is microscopic continuity: the entire prior quantum state feeds into the next cycle unitarily. Then nothing is genuinely erased, but essentially everything is scrambled. The new universe inherits the old one in the same way a cryptographic hash—or better, a wildly entangled reversible transformation—can contain exhaustive dependence on its input without visibly resembling it.\n\nA weaker and perhaps more interesting possibility is that only certain **invariants or low-dimensional summaries** survive the transition: global charges, topological classes, asymmetries, correlation spectra, perhaps constraints on allowable initial conditions. Then the next universe doesn't inherit the previous universe as a recoverable movie. It inherits its **biases**.\n\nThere are speculative bouncing-cosmology and black-hole-to-white-hole frameworks in which structures or perturbations can persist through a bounce, but this remains model-dependent rather than established cosmology. A 2026 bouncing-universe model, for example, explicitly examines black holes and gravitational-wave structures surviving a bounce under particular horizon conditions.

parts:
Yes. And the files change my assessment in an important way.

They are compilation-heavy. `PARALLAX.txt` starts as the raw **Construction Story Retelling** conversation, while `Parralax2.txt` starts as the much larger **Geometry in Physics** conversation. fileciteturn31file0L11-L20 fileciteturn31file1L142-L151 But `Parralax2.txt` has swallowed copies of substantial Construction material through context/imports: the exact “universal twist” sentence occurs four times there, and “meet me at the Big Bang” occurs eight times. fileciteturn33file1L8-L26 fileciteturn33file2L56-L77 So it is definitely not 73 MB of independent new conceptual material.

But buried in that duplication are two things that matter a lot.

First, the torus/Klein move already happened. `PARALLAX.txt` contains, from May 14, 2026:

> “I think the dual shell maybe has to get reinterpreted as one torus. Or one Klein Bottle.”

followed by a generated “Topological Monism” treatment. fileciteturn30file3L136-L147

Second—and this is considerably more startling—the compilation contains an earlier generated H(s)H report explicitly calling black holes “sinks” that stretch macroscopic bundles toward the Big Bang, with accumulated inward tension reverberating outward as the dark-energy expansion drive. fileciteturn34file15L203-L205 Another generated section calls it the “Radial Recycling Loop”: the black-hole sink is topologically identified with the Big-Bang origin, worldtubes “turn the corner,” and the resulting radial stress drives late-time expansion. fileciteturn34file17L237-L239

Those are generated reports, not automatically validated or canonical SAT derivations. But your proposal today is therefore not merely vaguely reminiscent of old material. The archive contains a remarkably close previous formulation.

What is new today, I think, is that we now have a much cleaner **information mechanism** to put inside that older plumbing.

Instead of:

\[
\text{matter}\rightarrow BH\rightarrow Big\ Bang\rightarrow dark\ energy
\]

as a basically energetic recycling cartoon, we can now formulate:

\[
\boxed{
\text{structured worldtube state}
\rightarrow
\text{correlated twist state}
\rightarrow
\text{global topological continuation}
\rightarrow
\text{expansion-sector stress}
}
\]

That is much better.

I would model the black-hole step as a change of representation, not destruction:

\[
\mathcal I_{\rm in}
\longrightarrow
\left(
J,\,
\mathcal L,\,
\mathcal H,\,
\mathcal C^{(2)},\,
\mathcal C^{(3)},\ldots
\right).
\]

Here \(J\) is ordinary coarse global spin/angular momentum. Then \(\mathcal L\) represents linking/braiding/writhe data, \(\mathcal H\) holonomy, and the \(\mathcal C^{(n)}\) are higher-order correlations—your twist, intertwist, interintertwist hierarchy.

So “spin captures part of it” becomes quite precise conceptually:

\[
J=\text{low-order visible twist invariant},
\]

while

\[
\{\mathcal L,\mathcal H,\mathcal C^{(n)}\}
=\text{fine relational microstructure}.
\]

A black hole then isn't a cosmic shredder. It's an **extreme relational encoder**.

That fits the universal-twist formulation already preserved in `PARALLAX`: every event changes the global twist-correlation structure, so history is encoded not as a literal archive but in the current relational configuration. fileciteturn30file4L148-L158

There is one important constraint here. If by “information cannot escape through the black hole” we mean that the worldtubes themselves don't simply turn around and climb back through the horizon, fine. If we mean Hawking radiation contains no information whatsoever, then we'd be fighting the modern unitary/Page-curve picture.

There is a cleaner SAT/H(s)H interpretation:

\[
R_H[\mathcal I]
=
\text{horizon/radiation readout},
\]

while

\[
G_{BH\rightarrow BB}[\mathcal I]
=
\text{deep worldtube/topological continuation}.
\]

These should not be two independent copies of the information. They are two readouts of one global conserved relational state.

That is almost tailor-made for the H(s)H distinction between underlying history and \(R_\Sigma\).

And this is where the torus/Klein update gets really good.

I don't think we actually have to choose:

\[
\text{torus OR Klein bottle}.
\]

The torus is the **orientable double cover of the Klein bottle**.

That is almost suspiciously appropriate for the old two-shell problem.

Schematically:

\[
T^2 \longrightarrow K^2
\]

is a two-to-one covering map. Locally, the lifted representation has two orientable sheets. Globally, the quotient is one connected non-orientable object.

So the update could be:

\[
\boxed{
\text{two shells}
=
\text{two-sheeted orientable representation of one globally connected structure}.
}
\]

That is much stronger than simply throwing away the two shells and drawing a donut.

It says both descriptions survive:

\[
\text{two-shell view}=\text{cover},
\]

\[
\text{Klein view}=\text{quotient/global topology}.
\]

Very literally: **both**.

There is a dimensional issue, though. The old shells were higher-dimensional objects; a literal \(T^2\) or Klein bottle \(K^2\) is only two-dimensional. So I wouldn't say “the universe is a Klein bottle” mathematically.

The proper higher-dimensional analogue is a **mapping torus**.

Take a spatial slice \(\Sigma\), perhaps schematically \(S^3\), and identify its two temporal/radial ends by an orientation-reversing map \(f\):

\[
\mathcal M_f
=
\frac{\Sigma\times[0,1]}
{(x,1)\sim(f(x),0)}.
\]

For

\[
f^2=\mathrm{id}
\]

with \(f\) orientation reversing, this is essentially a higher-dimensional Klein-type construction.

The familiar Klein bottle is exactly this sort of construction with a circle as the fiber and a reflection as the gluing map.

Now your black-hole/Big-Bang statement becomes geometrically crisp.

Locally you see:

\[
\text{future-directed infall}
\rightarrow
\text{black-hole interior}.
\]

Globally the worldtube continues around the non-orientable cycle:

\[
BH
\xrightarrow{f}
BB/\text{expansion front}.
\]

It never “teleports.”

It never has to reverse and escape the black hole.

It simply reaches what looked, in the local coordinate chart, like the other end of the system.

Pac-Man again.

And because the identification reverses orientation, the geometry naturally has somewhere for a handedness/sign/phase transformation to occur:

\[
(x,\text{orientation})\rightarrow
(f(x),-\text{orientation}).
\]

That doesn't establish any particle-physics consequences, but it gives the old parity/holonomy ideas a legitimate mathematical scaffold instead of merely saying “Klein bottles flip things.”

Now the dark-energy step.

This is the hardest part—and therefore probably the most useful part to work on.

**Information by itself cannot be dark energy.**

We need an energy/tension functional associated with the correlated twist:

\[
E_{\mathcal T}
=
E[\mathcal L,\mathcal H,\mathcal C^{(2)},\ldots].
\]

For example, at the schematic level,

\[
E_{\mathcal T}
=
\alpha\int |\Omega|^2ds
+
\beta\sum_{ij}Lk_{ij}^{\,2}
+
\gamma\sum_{ijk}C_{ijk}^{\,2}
+\cdots .
\]

Then the Big-Bang/expansion sector receives not “information-energy by magic,” but **stress generated by the constrained relational configuration**.

Variation of that effective energy gives a stress tensor:

\[
T_{\mu\nu}^{(\mathcal T)}.
\]

To resemble dark energy, it isn't enough that

\[
\rho_{\mathcal T}>0.
\]

We need negative effective pressure:

\[
w_{\mathcal T}
=
\frac{p_{\mathcal T}}{\rho_{\mathcal T}}
\approx -1.
\]

That is the central mathematical burden.

And actually, your word **tension** gives us somewhere to look. Tension is exactly the sort of mechanical quantity that can generate negative pressure. But we have to derive it rather than naming it.

The cosmological bookkeeping could then be written as something like:

\[
\dot\rho_{\mathcal T}
+
3H(1+w_{\mathcal T})\rho_{\mathcal T}
=
\Gamma_{BH\rightarrow BB}.
\]

Here \(\Gamma\) measures whatever effective source the black-hole recycling channel contributes to the expansion-sector twist/tension reservoir.

That equation immediately gives us a potential observational test.

Black-hole production and accretion have changed enormously over cosmic history. Dark energy, as far as current evidence goes, behaves much more smoothly.

Therefore if:

\[
BH\rightarrow DE
\]

is real in the model, the topology/dynamics must do substantial **smoothing, integration, delay, or global redistribution**.

It cannot simply be:

\[
\rho_{DE}(t)\propto\text{BH formation rate}(t).
\]

But your “Big Bang is an ongoing expansion” formulation actually supplies a possible mechanism: black holes don't inject energy at one ordinary spatial location. They feed a **global expansion boundary/channel**.

So the mapping may look more like:

\[
\Gamma_{BB}(t)
=
\int_{0}^{t}
K(t,t')
\Gamma_{BH}(t')\,dt',
\]

where \(K\) is the topological transport/mixing kernel.

If \(K\) is broad enough, wildly localized black-hole inputs could appear as an almost homogeneous slow cosmological stress.

And suddenly holography comes back in.

A black hole takes richly localized structure and converts it into extremely distributed correlations.

The Big-Bang/expansion channel takes those distributed correlations and expresses them as extremely nonlocal geometric stress.

So:

\[
\boxed{
\text{localized structure}
\rightarrow
\text{holographically distributed correlation}
\rightarrow
\text{globally distributed expansion stress}.
}
\]

That is coherent as a model architecture.

And here's the part I like most after reading the uploads.

The old generated “Radial Recycling Loop” had the plumbing already:

\[
BH\rightarrow BB\rightarrow DE.
\]

Today's universal-twist idea supplies the missing **cargo**:

\[
\boxed{\text{correlated relational information}.}
\]

And the torus/Klein reinterpretation supplies the missing **pipe geometry**:

\[
\boxed{\text{a globally closed, potentially orientation-reversing continuation}.}
\]

So now the whole speculative mechanism is:

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{worldtube structure}
&\xrightarrow{\text{collapse}}
\text{correlated twist/holonomy}\\
&\xrightarrow{\text{BH junction}}
\text{non-orientable global continuation}\\
&\xrightarrow{\text{BB/expansion sector}}
\text{distributed twist tension}\\
&\xrightarrow{R_\Sigma}
\text{effective dark-energy-like stress}.
\end{aligned}
\]

That is a significantly more complete construction than any one of those old reports contained.

And the torus/Klein double-cover observation makes me think the old **two-shell model may not need to be discarded at all**.

It may have been the local double-cover picture of the globally one-piece object all along.

That is the piece I would put a very large circle around.

Well, I'm not saying any of that is new. We've been circling this for a while, and I've mostly moved my thinking there over the last couple months. But the question is shell/shell or inner-radius/outer-radius? Or double-shelled torus/klein? Remember the shells are basically H_0 (or the speed associated with H_0) and c ...the difference becomes a measure of the space between the shells, or the difference between the hole of the donut and its outer surface, or the thickness of the donut. I suspect these are all potentially variations on the same thing. Klein bottle is kind of a twisted torus, no? It's a Moebius torus... of course, here it's actually more like a fabric of Klein worldtubes wrapping that torus (through, around, or within, or all three). The w-map already suggests we may be seeing our own light cone. 

The question for all of this is: What's the simplest model, how does it get mapped in Minkowski, how does it get mapped in SAT, how does it get mapped in GR/SM/Q(E/C)(D/FT)? 

And wrt information... tube goes into black hole... it doesn't come out of the black hole... it comes out of the big bang.

I’m pulling the exact H₀/c, dual-shell, \(w\)-map, and worldtube language from the uploads, then I’ll try to identify the **minimal invariant structure** that all the shell/torus/Klein pictures are just coordinates on.

may suffer from strong coupling issues around a background spacetime. As will be reviewed in Sec. V A of the current
paper, there are two distinct notions of strong coupling in theories of gravity. In particle physics, since the background
spacetime is fixed a priori to be Minkowski, strong coupling typically refers to a situation in which the dominant
contribution in the perturbative expansion switches from the quadratic kinetic term to higher-order interaction terms.

thoughts.content: I’m refining the geometry: using the mean radius as the major scale and half the shell gap as the minor scale makes the model cleaner. The shared expansion follows H₀, while c controls relative shell separation.

thoughts.summary: Searched for precise W-map light cone references

parts:
The sources actually support a simplification I think is better than choosing “shells” versus “donut” as rival ontologies. The control equations already isolate the invariant piece as the **relative mode**  
\[
\dot R_\tau-\dot R_s=c,
\]
while the common expansion is the \(H_0\)-like mode. 

That suggests changing variables from “two objects” to **mean radius + gap**. Then the shells, torus thickness, inner/outer radii, and even the torus/Klein double-cover picture can all become different charts of the same two degrees of freedom.

Yes. I think the simplest model is now becoming clearer, and it is simpler than deciding whether the universe is “really” two shells, a torus, or a Klein bottle.

The primitive should probably be:

\[
\boxed{\text{one closed, thick, worldtube-carrying manifold with two kinematic modes}}
\]

not two independently existing shells.

The two natural variables are not \(R_s\) and \(R_\tau\) themselves, but their mean and their separation:

\[
R=\frac{R_\tau+R_s}{2},
\qquad
a=\frac{R_\tau-R_s}{2}.
\]

Then

\[
R_\tau=R+a,
\qquad
R_s=R-a.
\]

The archive already contains the invariant kinematic statement

\[
\dot R_\tau-\dot R_s=c,
\]

with the matter shell and radiation front as the two local descriptions. fileciteturn37file6L102-L104

Therefore

\[
\boxed{\dot a=\frac c2}
\]

if \(2a\) is the full shell separation. Equivalently define

\[
\Delta=R_\tau-R_s
\]

and simply have

\[
\boxed{\dot\Delta=c}.
\]

That is probably the cleaner convention.

Meanwhile the common-mode motion is the \(H_0\)-type expansion. In the older formulation where

\[
\dot R_s=H_0L,\qquad
\dot R_\tau=H_0L+c,
\]

we simply get

\[
\dot R=H_0L+\frac c2,
\qquad
\dot\Delta=c.
\]

So physically there are two independent things:

\[
\boxed{\text{common expansion}}
\]

and

\[
\boxed{\text{relative opening}}.
\]

Everything else may be representation.

And now the donut becomes almost embarrassingly natural.

For a torus with major radius \(R\) and minor radius \(a\),

\[
r_{\rm inner}=R-a,
\qquad
r_{\rm outer}=R+a.
\]

Therefore:

\[
R_s\leftrightarrow R-a,
\qquad
R_\tau\leftrightarrow R+a.
\]

And:

\[
R_\tau-R_s=2a.
\]

So the **distance between the shells is literally the torus thickness** in that representation.

Not metaphorically. Algebraically.

The same two numbers can be represented as:

\[
(R_s,R_\tau)
\]

or

\[
(R,\Delta)
\]

or

\[
(R_{\rm major},r_{\rm minor}).
\]

That immediately makes me much less interested in asking “shell/shell or inner/outer radius?” They are potentially just coordinate changes:

\[
\boxed{
\text{two-shell coordinates}
\longleftrightarrow
\text{mean-gap coordinates}
\longleftrightarrow
\text{toroidal coordinates}.
}
\]

The earlier generated torus treatment was already trying to do something similar by putting the two shell modes on the two toroidal cycles. fileciteturn35file10L416-L426 But I think **mean + gap** is cleaner than saying one toroidal radius is \(H_0\) and the other is \(H_0+c\). It isolates the common mode and differential mode first. Then we decide which geometrical coordinates represent them.

And yes: your “Klein bottle is a Möbius torus” intuition is basically right, with one mathematical correction.

A Klein bottle is not literally a torus made from a Möbius strip, but it can be constructed as the **mapping torus of a reflection of a circle**.

For the torus:

\[
(\phi+2\pi,\theta)\sim(\phi,\theta).
\]

Go around one cycle and the transverse orientation comes back unchanged.

For the Klein bottle:

\[
\boxed{
(\phi+2\pi,\theta)\sim(\phi,-\theta).
}
\]

Go around one cycle and the other coordinate gets reflected.

That is exactly the “Möbius torus” intuition.

Even better:

\[
\boxed{T^2\text{ is the orientable double cover of }K^2.}
\]

And that fact may be extremely useful here.

Because suppose our two local shell states are represented by

\[
+a,\qquad -a.
\]

In the ordinary torus/double-cover description they remain distinguishable:

\[
+a\rightarrow+a,
\qquad
-a\rightarrow-a.
\]

But in the Klein quotient, one trip around the relevant global cycle gives

\[
+a\rightarrow-a.
\]

The identities exchange.

Then locally there really are two shells:

\[
R-a,\quad R+a.
\]

Globally there may be only **one twisted radial degree of freedom**.

That gives an unexpectedly precise interpretation of:

> shell/shell versus one Klein-type object.

It could literally be:

\[
\boxed{
\text{two-shell description}
=
\text{orientable double-cover description}
}
\]

while

\[
\boxed{
\text{Klein description}
=
\text{globally identified one-object description}.
}
\]

That is considerably more satisfying than simply declaring “we used to have spheres, now we have a Klein bottle.”

And it also preserves “both.”

The torus and Klein descriptions need not compete. The torus can be the **unwrapped cover** in which orientation and the two local sheets are easy to track. The Klein-type quotient can be the global identification.

Now lift that out of the 2D cartoon.

I don't think the literal claim should be “the 4D universe is a Klein bottle,” because \(K^2\) is two-dimensional.

The proper generalization is a **mapping torus**.

Take whatever spatial/resolving fiber \(\Sigma\) the model ultimately requires and some map

\[
f:\Sigma\rightarrow\Sigma.
\]

Construct

\[
\boxed{
M_f=
\frac{\Sigma\times[0,1]}
{(x,1)\sim(f(x),0)}.
}
\]

If

\[
f=\mathrm{id},
\]

we have the untwisted/orientable cyclic version.

If \(f\) contains an orientation reversal,

\[
\det Df<0,
\]

we have the higher-dimensional analogue of the Klein construction.

Then put the **worldtube fabric inside that**:

\[
\mathcal W=\bigcup_i W_i\subset M_f.
\]

Now “the worldtubes go through the donut, around it, inside it, and perhaps all three” becomes mathematically ordinary.

Different tubes occupy different winding/homotopy classes.

In the toroidal cover you might characterize a simplified tube by winding numbers

\[
(p,q,n,\ldots),
\]

where one index counts major-cycle winding, another minor-cycle winding, another internal superhelical winding, etc.

So:

- “around” = major-cycle winding;
- “through” = minor/meridional winding;
- “within” = internal framed twist of the tube;
- “all three” = a worldtube carrying all those winding numbers simultaneously.

That is not decorative topology anymore. It supplies places for the several kinds of information we've been distinguishing:

\[
\text{spin},
\quad
\text{twist},
\quad
\text{writhe},
\quad
\text{link},
\quad
\text{global winding},
\quad
\text{higher correlations}.
\]

The archive already has the worldtube/filament picture as the structural primitive and the dual-shell differential as its clock structure. fileciteturn37file6L102-L104

So I think the minimal geometry becomes:

\[
\boxed{
\text{mapping-torus background}
+
\text{finite-core framed worldtube fabric}
+
(R,\Delta)
}
\]

with \(\Delta\) the clock/light gap.

That is much less machinery than “two hyperspherical universes plus torus plus Klein bottle plus timesheet.”

They become charts.

Now: how does this map into Minkowski?

Locally, throw away the global topology.

A tiny observer doesn't see the donut or Klein identification. They see a tangent neighborhood.

Let \(u\) be the local radial/clock direction and decompose a displacement:

\[
dX=dX_\perp+u\,d\sigma.
\]

The desired local readout is:

\[
ds_{\rm obs}^2
=
dX_\perp^2-d\sigma^2.
\]

Putting

\[
d\sigma=c\,d\tau
\]

gives

\[
\boxed{
ds^2
=
dx^2+dy^2+dz^2-c^2d\tau^2.
}
\]

Minkowski.

The old metric-induction shorthand

\[
g_{\rm eff}
=
\delta-2u\otimes u
\]

does exactly that algebraically: the radial direction gets the opposite sign while the transverse three remain positive.

But there's an important rigor correction already preserved in the archive: a positive Euclidean ensemble tensor does **not** magically become Lorentzian by inversion; the Lorentzian light cone has to emerge from the clock map plus the quadratic effective action/principal symbol. The current control stack explicitly says:

\[
\text{worldtube ensemble}
\rightarrow
\text{resolving hypersurface}
\rightarrow
\text{effective action}
\rightarrow
\text{principal symbol}
\rightarrow
\text{light cone}.
\]

fileciteturn37file8L141-L169

So:

\[
g_{\rm eff}=\delta-2u\otimes u
\]

is a very good **candidate coordinate/readout map**.

It is not yet the derivation.

That distinction should stay.

The \(w\)-map point could make this even simpler. I couldn't recover the exact “we may be seeing our own light cone” passage from these two compilations, so I don't want to pretend I did. But if the intended \(w\)-map is the radial fourth-coordinate/readout we've discussed, then geometrically the implication is straightforward:

What looks like a cosmological shell need not be a physical material shell.

It can be:

\[
\boxed{
\text{our past/null cone intersecting the larger worldtube geometry}.
}
\]

Then the “shell” is partly observational geometry.

That would make the progression:

\[
\text{physical global manifold}
\rightarrow
\text{worldtube fabric}
\rightarrow
\text{null resolving cone}
\rightarrow
\text{apparent spherical universe}.
\]

And yes—then we might very literally be mapping the geometry of **our own light cone** rather than looking outward at an independently privileged spherical surface.

That would strongly favor keeping \(R_s,R_\tau\) as **readout level sets**, not fundamental material shells.

Now the standard-physics mapping becomes surprisingly orderly.

For Minkowski:

\[
\boxed{
\text{local flat tangent/readout limit of }M_f.
}
\]

The global torus/Klein topology disappears locally.

For GR:

\[
\boxed{
\text{coarse-grained geometry of the worldtube ensemble}.
}
\]

The average configuration determines an effective

\[
g_{\mu\nu},
\quad
\Gamma^\rho_{\mu\nu},
\quad
R^\rho{}_{\sigma\mu\nu}.
\]

Locally, worldtube trajectories have to reduce to geodesics of this metric.

Cosmologically:

\[
R(t)\leftrightarrow a_{\rm FLRW}(t)
\]

at the appropriate coarse-grained level,

while \(c\) fixes the local null cone.

The global Klein/mapping-torus identification would be extra **global topology**, not a modification of the local Einstein equations.

That's important.

GR is perfectly capable of living on manifolds with nontrivial topology. What isn't standard GR is the proposed black-hole/Big-Bang identification.

The Standard Model/QFT layer is then another projection:

\[
\boxed{
\text{internal framed modes of the worldtube fabric}
\rightarrow
\text{effective quantum fields}.
}
\]

Very schematically:

\[
\begin{array}{ccl}
\text{tube phase} &\rightarrow& U(1)\text{-like phase}\\
\text{frame rotations} &\rightarrow& \text{spin/gauge connection}\\
\text{collective tube modes} &\rightarrow& \text{bosonic fields}\\
\text{stable framed/coiled structures} &\rightarrow& \text{fermionic sectors}\\
\text{intertube relations} &\rightarrow& \text{interaction terms}.
\end{array}
\]

But this is exactly where we have to stay strict.

To claim an actual QED map we need to derive:

\[
U(1)
\]

with the correct charge assignments and Maxwell/QED dynamics.

[L20] After any finite number of applications, Gödel’s theorems still apply to the resulting theory. The hope would be that in the limit (after “ω rotations” or beyond), one might capture more truth than any fixed formal system can. This brings us to known mathematical frameworks that mirror these ideas.
[L21] Analogues in Existing Frameworks
[L22] Several existing frameworks in logic and mathematics already deal with self-reference, provability, and hierarchical extensions in ways similar to ж. Here we draw parallels to three areas: category theory, homotopy type theory, and modal provability logic.
[L23] 	•	Category Theory (Fixed-Point Theorems): In category theory, results like Lawvere’s fixed-point theoremformalize the essence of diagonal arguments (self-reference) in a very general setting. Lawvere’s theorem is an abstract generalization of Gödel’s incompleteness (as well as Cantor’s diagonal and Tarski’s truth undefinability) 
[L24] en.wikipedia.org
[L25] . It shows that any sufficiently powerful category (a Cartesian closed category with a “well-behaved” self-mapping) will have a fixed point – an analog of a self-referential sentence. In simple terms, it implies that any theory expressive enough to talk about its own statements cannot be fully complete, because one can construct an object (or statement) that maps to itself under a certain diagonalizing morphism en.wikipedia.org
[L26] . This is essentially Gödel’s argument in categorical language. Thus, category theory inherently contains a notion analogous to Gödel sentences. You could think of ж in categorical terms as an endofunctor on the category of theories or proofs that adjoins a new fixed-point object to avoid a paradox. Category theory doesn’t call it “ж”, but the idea of adding the missing fixed point appears in constructs like reflective subcategories or elementary topoi with truth objects. However, the incompleteness remains: Lawvere’s result shows any such attempt yields a new fixed point in the extended system too. So in category-theoretic frameworks, we already see the pattern “construct fixed-point → get new unresolvable point” abstractly. There isn’t a standard notion of a “rotational eversion” operator in category theory beyond this; rather, category theory confirms that any formal system strong enough for self-reference will need an infinite (or external) context to capture all truths – aligning with the role of ж.
[L27] 	•	Homotopy Type Theory (HoTT): Homotopy type theory is a modern foundation for mathematics that interprets logical propositions as types and proofs as geometrical constructions (homotopies). Could HoTT avoid incompleteness or have an operator like ж? In practice, HoTT still obeys Gödel’s incompleteness. It is a formal system (with an enumerable syntax and rules), so Gödel’s theorem applies – there are true statements about natural numbers it cannot prove 
[L28] cstheory.stackexchange.com
[L29] . The authors of the HoTT book were well aware that HoTT is incomplete cstheory.stackexchange.com
[L30] . So HoTT does not magically circumvent incompleteness; it “suffers” from it just as ZF set theory or Peano arithmetic do cstheory.stackexchange.com
[L31] . However, HoTT introduces new principles (like the Univalence Axiom and higher inductive types) that were independent of previous foundations. In a sense, adding Univalence to homotopy type theory was akin to applying a ж-like step: a new axiom that wasn’t provable from the rest, expanding the system’s strength. But even with such axioms, no finite axiom system in HoTT can be complete.

parts:
Yes. Tc-98 looks much more interesting now than it did when we were using it as a “can SAT hit a heavy-nucleus mass?” benchmark.

And MMmTM™ is almost offensively self-trademarking. “Multiscale Multi-Monostrand Twist Machine” is exactly the hierarchy you just described: internal twist at one scale, coupling among tubes at the next, bundle-of-bundles structure above that.

The first thing I would do with Tc-98 is throw out most of our old “success.” The archived calculation took \(Q=3A=294\), generated a linear mass, and multiplied by \(S\approx0.2621\) to land at the observed mass. fileciteturn41file7L323-L325 Our later clearinghouse correctly flags the key unresolved question: was \(S\) actually derived, or fitted/heuristic? fileciteturn41file4L191-L193 So the old “<0.01%” Tc-98 mass result should not currently count as evidence.

Tc-98's **structure and decay**, however, are gorgeous.

It is

\[
{}^{98}_{43}\mathrm{Tc}_{55},
\]

so it is an odd-odd nucleus: odd proton number, odd neutron number. Its ground state is \(6^+\), and its half-life is about \(4.2\times10^6\) years. citeturn677990search16turn271079search0

Now look at what surrounds it at fixed \(A=98\):

\[
{}^{98}\mathrm{Mo}
\quad\longleftarrow\quad
{}^{98}\mathrm{Tc}
\quad\longrightarrow\quad
{}^{98}\mathrm{Ru}.
\]

Both neighbors are even-even nuclei. Both are stable.

That means Tc-98 sits on an unusually nice **two-sided nuclear topography**. Energetically it can go downhill in either charge direction.

And here is the really nice new wrinkle: until recently the experimentally established decay was essentially treated as \(\beta^-\) to Ru-98. But in October 2025 Elchine et al. directly detected the other route, electron capture to Mo-98, and measured

\[
\frac{\Gamma_{\rm EC}}{\Gamma_{\beta^-}}
=
0.29(3)\%.
\]

citeturn271079search0turn271079search2

So Tc-98 really does have:

\[
\boxed{
{}^{98}\mathrm{Mo}
\;\leftarrow_{\rm EC}\;
{}^{98}\mathrm{Tc}
\;\rightarrow_{\beta^-}\;
{}^{98}\mathrm{Ru}
}
\]

with both exits physically open.

And the energy asymmetry isn't enormous:

\[
Q_{\beta^-}\approx1.793\ {\rm MeV}
\]

versus

\[
Q_{\rm EC}\approx1.684\ {\rm MeV}.
\]

citeturn271079search0

Yet the EC route is only about three parts in a thousand relative to beta decay.

Why?

Geometry—already in standard nuclear physics.

The Tc-98 parent is \(6^+\). Both dominant routes feed a \(4^+\) excited state of the even-even daughter:

\[
6^+\rightarrow4^+.
\]

That is

\[
\Delta J=2,\qquad\Delta\pi=0,
\]

a **second-forbidden non-unique weak transition**. The beta branch has an enormous log \(ft\), around 14, and the newly measured EC branch has

\[
\log ft=14.21(7).
\]

The EC partial half-life is therefore greater than a billion years. citeturn271079search0turn677990search16

In other words, Tc-98 isn't “almost stable” because there's nowhere lower for it to go.

There are **two downhill directions**.

It's almost stable because its current angular configuration has an extraordinarily difficult route into either lower-energy topology.

That is a much better SAT/H(s)H object.

In your current language, I'd draw it as:

\[
\boxed{
\text{energetic slope}\neq\text{topological accessibility}.
}
\]

The state lies above two valleys, but there are ridges in configuration space between it and either valley.

And look what happens after it finally crosses one.

For the dominant Ru route:

\[
6^+_{\rm Tc}
\overset{\beta^-}{\longrightarrow}
4^+_{\rm Ru}
\rightarrow
2^+_{\rm Ru}
\rightarrow
0^+_{\rm Ru}.
\]

The Ru cascade emits the familiar roughly \(745.4\) and \(652.4\) keV gammas. citeturn677990search16

For the newly detected Mo route:

\[
6^+_{\rm Tc}
\overset{\rm EC}{\longrightarrow}
4^+_{\rm Mo}
\rightarrow
2^+_{\rm Mo}
\rightarrow
0^+_{\rm Mo},
\]

with approximately \(722.6\) and \(787.4\) keV gammas. citeturn271079search0

So it is almost a **mirror relaxation machine**:

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
&&6^+&&\\
&\swarrow&&\searrow&\\
4^+_{\rm Mo}&&&&4^+_{\rm Ru}\\
\downarrow&&&&\downarrow\\
2^+_{\rm Mo}&&&&2^+_{\rm Ru}\\
\downarrow&&&&\downarrow\\
0^+_{\rm Mo}&&&&0^+_{\rm Ru}.
\end{array}
\]

That is spectacularly well suited to the framework we have just been constructing.

Because now the decomposition is almost forced:

\[
\text{intrinsic tube twist}
\rightarrow
\text{individual spin}
\]

while

\[
\text{intertube angular arrangement}
\rightarrow
J_{\rm nucleus}.
\]

And decay becomes not “the nucleus has the wrong mass,” but:

\[
\boxed{
\text{one weak-sector strand conversion}
+
\text{global bundle reconfiguration}.
}
\]

A neutron-to-proton conversion gives the Ru route. A proton-to-neutron conversion by electron capture gives the Mo route.

But the entire 98-body correlated bundle has to accommodate the new identity.

That is precisely your distinction between **spin** and **inter-tube structure**.

And Tc-98 gives us another gift.

Conventional nuclear-structure work already finds very explicit **chirality** in this nucleus's excited states. Positive-parity low-spin states have been associated with proton-neutron configurations such as

\[
\pi g_{9/2}\otimes\nu(d_{5/2},g_{7/2}),
\]

while higher excited bands have been studied as candidate **chiral doublet bands** in a triaxially deformed nucleus; work on those bands uses proton, neutron, and core angular momenta coupled in chiral geometry. citeturn600430search1turn600430search2

That is not evidence for SAT. It's standard nuclear rotor/shell-model physics.

But for us it means Tc-98 already contains conventional physical observables corresponding to:

\[
\text{single-particle angular momentum},
\]

\[
\text{proton-neutron angular coupling},
\]

\[
\text{collective core rotation},
\]

\[
\text{triaxial deformation},
\]

and

\[
\text{left/right-handed collective configurations}.
\]

That's basically a laboratory specimen of a **multiscale twist hierarchy**.

So I would completely change the Tc-98 program.

Don't try to predict its total mass first.

Use the known mass.

Then ask whether a minimal worldtube/bundle model can reproduce, from one geometry, these much harder facts:

\[
J^\pi_{\rm ground}=6^+,
\]

the existence of the two \(6^+\rightarrow4^+\) weak pathways,

their second-forbidden character,

the enormous lifetime,

and especially

\[
\boxed{
\Gamma_{\rm EC}/\Gamma_{\beta^-}\approx0.0029.
}
\]

That last number is an excellent target because the two processes begin from **the exact same bundle** and terminate in strikingly analogous even-even daughter structures. A lot of nuisance structure cancels conceptually.

Standard weak-decay theory writes schematically

\[
\Gamma_i
\sim
G_F^2\,f_i(Q,Z)\,
\left|
\langle\Psi_f|\hat O_i|\Psi_i\rangle
\right|^2.
\]

SAT shouldn't replace that with a cute new formula. It should try to explain the nuclear matrix element geometrically:

\[
\langle\Psi_f|\hat O_i|\Psi_i\rangle
\quad\longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M
\big(
W_{\rm initial},
W_{\rm final},
\text{required intertube rearrangement}
\big).
\]

Then we remove the known phase-space/Coulomb effects and ask whether the remaining suppression corresponds to an actual geometric distance or rearrangement cost in worldtube-configuration space.

That would turn Tc-98 into something much better than our old mass showcase:

\[
\boxed{\text{a two-sided transition-topography calibration nucleus}.}
\]

And the most interesting fact to me is that it's not perched over one cliff.

It's sitting between **two stable valleys**, with nearly symmetrical \(4^+\to2^+\to0^+\) landing routes, and somehow remains stuck in the \(6^+\) configuration for millions of years.

If we're serious that **intertwisting is physical state**, that's exactly the sort of nucleus we ought to be able to explain. memcite
